maa-definition.title: Maass forms and the hyperbolic Laplacian

questions.q: Which equation does a Maass form $f:\mathbb{H}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfy that a holomorphic modular form does NOT?
choices: the eigenvalue equation $\Delta f=\lambda f$ for the hyperbolic Laplacian $\Delta=-y^2(\partial_x^2+\partial_y^2)$
the modular transformation law $f(\gamma z)=(cz+d)^k f(z)$
questions.explain: Both share $\Gamma$-invariance/automorphy, but the holomorphic side imposes $\partial_{\bar z}f=0$ while the Maass side imposes a second-order elliptic eigenvalue PDE. A weight-zero Maass form is real-analytic but generically NOT holomorphic — its $\bar\partial f$ is non-zero, balanced by $\partial f$ to keep $\Delta f=\lambda f$.

questions.q: Maass eigenvalues are usually written $\lambda=\tfrac14+r^2$. If a Maass form has spectral parameter $r=4$, what is its Laplacian eigenvalue $\lambda$?
questions.explain: $\lambda=1/4+r^2=1/4+16=16.25$. The shift by $1/4$ is chosen so that the Selberg conjecture $\lambda\ge 1/4$ becomes the cleaner statement '$r$ is real'.

questions.q: A Maass cusp form on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$ has Fourier expansion at the cusp $\infty$ involving:
choices: powers of $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$ as in the holomorphic case
Bessel functions $K_{ir}(2\pi|n|y)$ multiplied by $\sqrt{y}\,e^{2\pi i n x}$
questions.explain: The Laplacian eigenvalue equation separates in $(x,y)$, and the only solution that decays at $y\to\infty$ for nonzero frequency is the modified Bessel function $K_{ir}(2\pi|n|y)$. The expansion $f(z)=\sum_{n\ne 0}a_f(n)\sqrt{y}\,K_{ir}(2\pi|n|y)e^{2\pi i n x}$ replaces the holomorphic $q$-expansion.

questions.q: The orthogonal decomposition of $L^2(\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H})$ for a non-cocompact congruence $\Gamma$ has three pieces. Which one is parameterised by a continuous variable on the line $\Re s=\tfrac12$?
questions.explain: $L^2_{\mathrm{cusp}}$ is a discrete countable sum of Laplacian eigenspaces; $L^2_{\mathrm{res}}$ is finite-dimensional (constants plus residues at simple poles in $(\tfrac12,1]$); only $L^2_{\mathrm{Eis}}$ is a direct integral of Eisenstein eigenpackets along $\Re s=\tfrac12$.

questions.q: Which statements about cuspidal Maass forms are TRUE?
choices: they vanish at every cusp (zeroth Fourier coefficient at each cusp is zero)
questions.explain: Smoothness, $\Delta$-eigen, cusp-vanishing, and $L^2$-ness are the defining package. Finite-dimensionality is FALSE: by the Weyl law there are infinitely many cuspidal eigenvalues, and their density is $\sim\mathrm{vol}/(4\pi)\cdot T$ as $T\to\infty$.

questions.q: On the modular surface $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$, the residual spectrum $L^2_{\mathrm{res}}$ consists of:
choices: all cusp forms with eigenvalue below $\tfrac14$
an infinite-dimensional space spanned by Eisenstein residues at every pole
questions.explain: For $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, $E(z,s)$ has a single simple pole in $\Re s>\tfrac12$ at $s=1$ with residue $3/\pi$ (a constant). So $L^2_{\mathrm{res}}$ is one-dimensional, spanned by $1$. Higher-rank groups can have richer residual spectra.

questions.q: Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture states that for any congruence subgroup $\Gamma$ of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, the lowest non-zero Laplacian eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ on cusp forms satisfies:
questions.explain: The conjectured bound is $\lambda_1\ge 1/4$, equivalently the spectral parameter $r$ is real (no exceptional eigenvalues). Selberg himself proved $\lambda_1\ge 3/16$ in 1965.

questions.q: If a Maass cusp form on a non-congruence subgroup has eigenvalue $\lambda=0.21$, what is its spectral parameter $r$ (in absolute value, taking $r\in i\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ as imaginary)? Give $|r|$ to 3 decimals.
questions.explain: $\lambda=1/4+r^2=0.21$ gives $r^2=-0.04$, i.e. $r=\pm 0.2 i$ — purely imaginary, an EXCEPTIONAL eigenvalue below $1/4$. Selberg conjectures these don't occur for congruence groups.

questions.q: The current best known unconditional bound on $\lambda_1$ for congruence subgroups is:
questions.explain: Kim–Sarnak (2003) gives $\lambda_1\ge 975/4096\approx 0.2380$, derived from Kim–Shahidi's sym$^4$ functoriality result on $\mathrm{GL}_2$. Still strictly below $1/4=0.25$; the conjecture itself is open.

questions.q: The non-holomorphic Eisenstein series $E(z,s)=\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_\infty\backslash\Gamma}(\Im\gamma z)^s$ converges absolutely for:
questions.explain: The sum is essentially $\sum_{(c,d)=1}|cz+d|^{-2s}$, dominated by $\sum(c^2+d^2)^{-s}$, which converges for $\Re s>1$. Selberg's analytic continuation extends $E(z,s)$ meromorphically to all of $\mathbb{C}$.

questions.q: $E(z,s)$ is a Laplacian eigenfunction with eigenvalue:
questions.explain: Direct computation: $\Delta y^s=-y^2\partial_y^2(y^s)=-s(s-1)y^s=s(1-s)y^s$. The whole sum inherits the eigenvalue $s(1-s)$. Substituting $s=1/2+ir$ gives $s(1-s)=1/4+r^2$, matching the Maass-form normalization.

questions.q: The constant term in the Fourier expansion of $E(z,s)$ at $\infty$ is $y^s+\phi(s)y^{1-s}$. For $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, the scattering coefficient $\phi(s)$ equals:
questions.explain: Unfolding the sum yields $\phi(s)=\sqrt{\pi}\Gamma(s-1/2)\zeta(2s-1)/(\Gamma(s)\zeta(2s))$. The functional equation $E(z,s)=\phi(s)E(z,1-s)$ then encodes the functional equation of $\zeta(s)$ — historically Riemann's continuation re-derived spectrally.

questions.q: For a Hecke eigenform Maass cusp form $f$, the $L$-function $L(s,f)=\sum_{n\ge 1}a_f(n)n^{-s}$ has an Euler product. The local factor at an unramified prime $p$ is:
questions.explain: Just like a weight-$k$ holomorphic eigenform but with weight zero: $L_p(s,f)=(1-a_f(p)p^{-s}+p^{-2s})^{-1}$. The exponent on the $p^{-2s}$ tail is $0$ (vs. $k-1$ in the holomorphic case) — Maass forms have weight zero, no $p^{k-1}$ shift.

questions.q: The Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture for Maass cusp forms says $|a_f(p)|\le ?$ at every unramified prime $p$:
questions.explain: $|a_f(p)|\le 2$ — the same bound as Deligne's theorem for holomorphic eigenforms (where $|a_f(p)|\le 2p^{(k-1)/2}$, so weight-zero gives $\le 2$). For Maass forms the conjecture is OPEN; current record Kim–Sarnak gives $|a_f(p)|\le 2p^{7/64}\approx 2p^{0.109}$.

questions.q: The functional equation for a Maass cusp form $f$ on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ relates $\Lambda(s,f)=\pi^{-s}\Gamma(\tfrac{s+\epsilon+ir}{2})\Gamma(\tfrac{s+\epsilon-ir}{2})L(s,f)$ to $\Lambda(1-s,f)$ (with $\epsilon=0$ for an even form, $1$ for odd). The center of the critical strip is $s=?$
questions.explain: The functional equation is $\Lambda(s,f)=\pm\Lambda(1-s,f)$, fixing the center at $s=1/2$. This is the same line on which the Eisenstein continuous spectrum lives — not a coincidence, since the Mellin transform of the Whittaker model produces $\Lambda(s,f)$.

maa-trace-formula.title: Selberg trace formula and the Weyl law

questions.q: The Selberg trace formula is, schematically, an identity equating:
choices: a sum over primes with a sum over zeros of $\zeta$
a spectral sum $\sum_j h(r_j)$ with a geometric sum over closed geodesics on $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}$
a sum over irreducible characters with a sum over conjugacy classes
a sum over modular forms with a sum over Hecke operators
questions.explain: Spectral side: $\sum_j h(r_j)$ over Laplacian eigenvalues $1/4+r_j^2$ (plus an Eisenstein integral). Geometric side: identity contribution + sum over $\Gamma$-conjugacy classes, where hyperbolic classes contribute terms indexed by closed geodesics. Number-theoretic analog of Poisson summation.

questions.q: The Weyl law for the modular surface $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$ (volume $\pi/3$) says $\#\{j:\lambda_j\le T\}\sim\mathrm{vol}\cdot T/(4\pi)$. To three decimals, what is the leading coefficient $\mathrm{vol}/(4\pi)$?
questions.explain: $\mathrm{vol}(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H})=\pi/3$, so $\mathrm{vol}/(4\pi)=1/12\approx 0.0833$. The first cuspidal eigenvalue $\lambda_1\approx 91.14$ is consistent: by $T=91.14$ the Weyl count predicts $\sim 7.6$ eigenvalues, in line with computation.

questions.q: An immediate Selberg-trace consequence is the prime geodesic theorem $\#\{\gamma:\ell(\gamma)\le X\}\sim ?$ as $X\to\infty$, where $\ell(\gamma)$ is the length of a primitive closed geodesic on $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}$.
questions.explain: The prime geodesic theorem gives $\#\{\gamma:\ell(\gamma)\le X\}\sim e^X/X$ — exact analog of the prime number theorem $\pi(N)\sim N/\log N$ under the substitution $N=e^X$. Closed geodesics on $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}$ play the role of primes; the trace formula is the spectral lever.
